title: A map of your practice
description: Where your practice stands on the ladder, which signs show that one-to-one work has become a ceiling, what the client really gets, and where your competence ends.

units.title: Where I stand on the ladder
Through the client's eyes: what they get

objectives.text: Describe your practice by the three axes of the ladder: step, channel and event class
Tell apart, in your own practice, the signs of “time to step up” from the signs of “too early”
For each client, separate what they get from the method and what they get from their relationship with you
Name the signs at which a practitioner stops and refers the client on, and draw up your own referral list

checks.question: One-to-one sessions once a week, in person and by video. How do you describe this by the axes of the ladder?
options: One to one · in person and online · regular
One to a few · in person · regular
checks.explain: There is one person in front of you — the “one to one” step. Meetings happen both in the room and by video — two channels. They repeat every week with no end of a cycle — the “regular” class (u1, “Three axes of the ladder”).

checks.question: Which of these signs says “too early” rather than “time to step up”?
options: Clients come back and bring friends
The same questions repeat from person to person
You cannot explain your approach in five minutes
There are almost no free hours left in your week
checks.explain: If the approach cannot be explained in five minutes, the method is not yet separated from you. It is too early to step up: first the method, then the step (u2, “Two lists of signs”).

checks.question: A client says: “It just feels good with you.” Which column of the map does this belong to?
options: None: it is just a compliment
checks.explain: This is the value of the relationship — the strength of the step. It becomes a ceiling when there is nothing to name in the “from the method” column (u3, “Two columns”).

checks.question: What does the ICF guide call the main sign that it is time to refer a client to a therapist?
options: The client cried in a session
For weeks the problem has been getting in the way of the client's daily life
The client missed two sessions in a row
The practitioner feels awkward talking to the client about their life
checks.explain: The main indicator in the ICF guide is daily functioning: self-care, work, home, leisure — and that it lasts for weeks. One episode of tears is not a sign (u4, “Signs to stop”).
